From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Context depth qualification + prompt suite — post-discovery next steps

Hi Elena / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can validate model fit against your visit-history summarization workflow: 

Summary of needs (from our call):
- Summarize multi-visit EHR notes (up to ~10k tokens) into a concise clinical timeline and problem list.
- High factual fidelity (low hallucination), preserve negations and dates.
- Integration constraints: streaming preferred, latency target ~600ms P50 for 1–2k token prompts, batch inference acceptable for larger background aggregation.

Immediate asks / proposal:
1) Baseline eval: Redwood run (sample set you provide) across three model candidates and our prompt permutations. We’ll produce ROUGE, entity-factuality (clinic-coded), and QA-based hallucination metrics.
2) Provide the sample file you mentioned (de-identified EHR exports) — we can run an initial 100-record pilot.
3) Kick off a 2-week technical pilot: Redwood supplies prompt suite + benchmark scripts, MedArchive signs off on evaluation metrics and privacy checklist.

Recommended models for the pilot (initial suggestions):
- rw_infer-13b-long-v2 (cost-effective long-context baseline)
- rw_infer-13b-q4f-long (quantized variant for cost/cpu tradeoff)
- rw_infer-70b-long-pro (higher-fidelity reference for clinical fidelity)

I attached a draft prompt_suite_v1.jsonl with 6 canonical prompt patterns (summary, timeline, problem-list, visit-extract, follow-up suggestions, evidence citations). Also attached: mutual_action_plan_MedArchive_v1.pdf and a sample record you dropped on the call (we redacted obvious PII).

Next steps: if this plan sounds good, reply with the dataset link (or drop to my Drive), and I’ll loop our ML lead (Neha) to propose evaluation cadence and target metrics.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Karthik — this looks like a good plan. A couple clarifications before we hand off the full sample: 

- On truncation: our current pipeline concatenates note text by visit chronologically; typical payloads are 3–8k tokens, but we have some edge cases up to ~12k. Curious how your prefix/KV caching would affect the summary if the beginning of the record is pushed out of context. Would running the model in a sliding-window with overlap + a final synthesis prompt be part of your recommended approach?

- We care a lot about citation fidelity: when the model lists medications or events, we need source snippets (anchors) and a confidence indicator for each extracted event. Is that part of the pilot output?

I attached a small (de-identified) record we can use for the initial run. If everything looks reasonable, I’ll loop in procurement (Sara Nguyen) to align on timelines/pricing.

—Elena
Director of Product, MedArchive
elena@medarchive.com

Attachment: medarchive_sample_record_20270912.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@medarchive.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 02:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Context depth qualification + prompt suite — post-discovery next steps

Hi Elena — great questions. Some quick technical answers and what we’ll include in the pilot deliverables: 

Short answers:
- Truncation / long-history handling: we recommend two parallel paths for the pilot: (A) RW long-context models (rw_infer-13b-long-v2 / rw_infer-70b-long-pro) which support 32k-ish context with prefix caching and KV reuse; and (B) a hybrid sliding-window + synthesis approach where we chunk visits (~4k tokens windows, 20% overlap), generate per-window extracts, then run a final synthesis prompt that merges deduped facts. The hybrid approach is a good cost/accuracy tradeoff for very long records.
- Anchoring & citations: we’ll return source spans for each extracted event (start token, end token, snippet) and include a lightweight confidence score (calibrated by our QA probe). That will be part of the benchmark output.

Pilot eval plan (what Redwood will run):
1) Dataset: 100 de-identified records (MedArchive provides).
2) Models: rw_infer-13b-long-v2 (baseline), rw_infer-13b-q4f-long (cost baseline), rw_infer-70b-long-pro (high-fidelity).
3) Prompt permutations: we’ll run 6 canonical prompts from the provided suite + 3 targeted probe prompts for negation/date handling.
4) Inference modes:
   - Full-context (single-pass) for records <= 16k tokens
   - Sliding-window + synthesis for records > 16k tokens (4k window, 20% overlap)
5) Metrics: ROUGE-L, entity recall/precision on problem-list & meds, Factuality via human adjudication on 20 QA pairs per record, hallucination rate (% of assertions without source-span).
6) Output: results CSV (attached example long_context_benchmarks_20270912.csv), per-record JSON with anchors, and a short write-up with recommendations on model choice and quantization profile.

Logistics / timeline:
- We can ingest the 100-record sample within 3 business days of receiving the files.
- Initial bench run and report: 7 business days after ingestion.
- Optional two-week expansion pilot (if you want to iterate prompts or add more records).

Cost note: using rw_infer-70b-long-pro as the reference will increase token-cost by ~3–4x vs the 13b baseline; we’ll provide a cost forecast once we know your expected monthly volume. The quantized 13b (q4f) typically gives ~30–45% cost savings at modest quality loss — we’ll quantify during the run.

We’ll include per-assertion anchors and a confidence indicator in the deliverable CSV so you can wire them into your downstream validation.

I’ll kick off the ingestion process as soon as you confirm the S3/Drive link.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Lead Applied ML — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: long_context_benchmarks_20270912.csv, prompt_suite_v1.jsonl
